content.text:
The campaign ran from 18 December to the end of 31 December (UK time) and stopped on schedule. It spent **$432.46 of your $450**, so it stayed under budget, and nothing is running now.

## Recap

| | Spend | Impressions | Link clicks | Cost per click |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Total** | **$432.46** | **393,706** | **182** | **$2.38** |

That's about 1 link click for every 2,160 impressions.

**By post:**
- **Post 1** ("New Year's resolution: read more…"): $248.50, 104 clicks, $2.39 per click
- **Post 2** ("£0. Thirty seconds…"): $183.96, 78 clicks, $2.36 per click

**By audience** (all UK, 18+):
- **People searching for or posting about** library, libraries, books, reading or "read more": $219.20, 93 clicks
- **People interested in** education or parenting: $213.26, 89 clicks

The strongest single ad was Post 1 shown to the library and reading audience: 65 clicks for $153.82. Still, every combination came in at $2.34–$2.43 per click, so no ad was clearly worse than the others. That's why I didn't pause any of them. The only change I made was on 23 December, when I raised the daily spending limits a little so the full budget could be used before the end. It still finished $17.54 under.

## Notes
- **Sign-ups:** There's no X pixel on the site, so X can't see whether anyone signed. These 182 clicks are visits to the petition page. Your own figures will show how many turned into signatures, volunteers or newsletter sign-ups.
- **Rules:** Both posts were approved for all four ads and stayed approved the whole time. Every ad was limited to the UK and to people aged 18 and over, and used only the targeting X allows for political campaigning ads.
- **Next time:** If you run this again, start with Post 1 for the library and reading audience. Also, putting X's pixel on the "thank you" page would let X aim for actual signatures rather than just clicks.

Good luck with the spring presentations. 📚
